conviction_note: The print turns on the first FY27 guide. Counterparties that reported after Woodward last spoke mostly point to a slower FY27: TransDigm guided every channel down on Nov 10 and cited softer traffic, and Safran's Q3 LEAP deliveries grew only 5% with spare-part growth slowing. GE Aerospace pulls the other way, with spare parts up more than 20% and low-double-digit 2027 services. Against that, the stock is already 27% off its high, fell 13.9% in the week after the Q3 beat-and-raise and another 6.5% in the last five sessions, and short interest is low, while Woodward's last initial guide (FY26, 7-12% growth, ended at 20-23%) was conservative and the stock was bought +12.4%. I net this to p_up 48 on a ~10% absolute move, so -0.4. The findings sum to -0.5 and agree in sign with the scaled number, and both are small because the FY27 bar has only one estimate source.
bar: Q4 FY26 consensus adj EPS $2.50 on ~$1.13B revenue (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-11, https://finviz.com/news/420898/woodward-closes-a-record-year-as-fading-tailwinds-put-its-fiscal-2027-outlook-on-trial ; Benzinga forecasts page https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WWD/earnings-forecasts shows the same $2.50/$1.13B). Company guide: FY26 adj EPS $9.30-9.50 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108312/000117184326005009/exh_991.htm). YTD adj EPS is 2.17+2.27+2.52 = $6.96, so the guide implies Q4 $2.34-2.54 (midpoint $2.44), and the $2.50 consensus sits in the top third of that. DISPUTE: the same preview gives a FY consensus of $9.34, which implies a Q4 of $2.38 and not $2.50, so the Q4 bar is internally inconsistent. The FY27 bar, which is the line that matters, has ONE source: Zacks FY27 EPS $10.30 (~+10% y/y), from search snippets of marketbeat/Zacks items. No company FY27 framework exists. Every finding is capped small for that reason.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.08M shares, 1.2 days to cover as of 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/wwd), and about 1.1M shares, 1.9 days, falling, as of 2026-10-05 (https://equibles.com/stocks/wwd/summary). That is under 2% of ~60M shares, so the short is not crowded and a squeeze is no mechanism here. Baseline: event implied move 9.63% (straddle 10.14%, ATM IV 139%). The 25-delta skew of 43.3 vol points was rejected as implausible, but it points the same way as a put/call open-interest ratio of 14.1 on 3,607 contracts, so options holders are paying heavily for downside. Tape: spot 316.52, 5d -6.51%, 20d -2.65%, -27.5% from the 52-week high of $450.92 (2026-06-25), about 8.5% below the 200-day. Earnings Whispers sentiment is 'barely positive', down from solidly bullish before Q3.

findings.finding: TransDigm's FY27 guide (Nov 10, after Woodward last spoke) slows every channel: commercial aftermarket to high single digits from ~14% in FY26, commercial OEM to high single/low double digits from ~15%, defense to high single digits from 10%. TDG tied the aftermarket slowdown to softer RPKs on elevated oil prices and Middle East tension, its EPS guide of $47.09-47.94 was below the $48.66 consensus, and its shares fell ~4%. Woodward's commercial services line was $268M (+24%) of $709M aerospace sales in Q3, and consensus FY27 (Zacks $10.30, ~+10%) assumes continued growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The initial-guide print of 2025-11-24 moved +12.44% on a conservative FY26 guide. The Q3 FY26 print (2026-07-29), where aftermarket growth decelerated to 24% from 36% and 50%, moved -7.56%, and -13.9% over the week.
findings.why_not_priced: WWD is down ~6.5% in five sessions and well below its 200-day, so some of the read-across is probably in the price. But no Woodward-specific FY27 estimate revision since TDG is visible: the only FY27 number found is Zacks's $10.30, and the preview frames the guide as an open test. If the market had fully priced a TDG-style aftermarket step-down, FY27 consensus would have been cut and the post-print implied move would be lower than 9.6%.
findings.independence: Partly corroborated by Safran's slowing spare parts and Q3 LEAP growth (https://www.safran-group.com/pressroom/safran-reports-its-third-quarter-2026-revenue-2026-10-23). Contradicted in part by GE Aerospace's spare parts >20% and low-double-digit 2027 services (https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-announces-third-quarter-2026-results). TDG is a peer, not a counterparty, and its aftermarket mix differs (more legacy/proprietary parts), so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: Safran's Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep, the same quarter as Woodward's fiscal Q4) shows 535 LEAP deliveries, +5% y/y against +26% for the nine months, a spare-engine ratio 'normalizing' versus H1, and slowing spare-parts growth, with the FY guide only confirmed. Woodward supplies LEAP fuel systems, and its commercial OEM grew +34% in Q3. A ~5% LEAP volume quarter points to slower Woodward commercial OEM growth in Q4 and a more modest OEM ramp into FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Commercial OEM has been the growth line (+34% in Q3). The baseline has no record of a print where it missed. The Q3 print was sold despite OEM strength.
findings.why_not_priced: Safran is a direct counterparty (via CFM) whose quarter matches Woodward's Q4 exactly, and it reported after Woodward last spoke. Q4 consensus ($1.13B, +13.5% y/y) already shows a slowdown, so the Q4 effect lands largely inside the guided range. The open question is the FY27 OEM growth assumption, which is unsourced.
findings.independence: Counterparty primary document. GE's Q3 also showed LEAP deliveries +5% in the quarter (https://www.geaerospace.com/news/investor-relations/ir-updates/ge-aerospace-releases-its-3q26-results), which is the same CFM fact seen from the other partner, so the two count once.

findings.finding: GE Aerospace's Q3 2026 (Oct 20) offsets the peers: commercial engines & services revenue +21%, services +17%, spare parts revenue >20%, LEAP shop visits >40%, 2026 guide raised, and 2027 commercial services growth framed as low double digits. Woodward's aerospace aftermarket rides LEAP/CFM56 shop visits, and this is the largest counterparty to speak after Woodward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Woodward's aftermarket line has decelerated three quarters running (50% to 36% to 24%) and the Q3 print was sold. A stabilisation has not yet been tested in the reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: WWD has drifted lower since GE reported, so the market has weighted TDG's caution over GE's strength for WWD. If GE's read had been priced into WWD, WWD would not be at a new post-Q3 low into the print.
findings.independence: Second-hand summary of GE's 2027 framing via Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/node/62464248). It runs against the TDG finding, and the two are not merged because they are different companies with different mixes.

findings.finding: On Q4 itself Woodward has beaten consensus EPS in every quarter of FY26 (Q2 $2.27, +13.5% vs Zacks; Q3 $2.52 vs $2.39), and Q3 FY26 sales were $1.11B, +21%. The Q4 consensus of $2.50 sits near the top of the guide-implied range ($2.34-2.54), and management guided Q4 industrial margins back toward first-half levels (~19% FY) with China on-highway near zero. A modest EPS beat is the base case, but the bar is disputed ($9.34 FY consensus implies $2.38).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This stock sold its Q3 beat-and-raise (-7.56% on the day, -13.9% on the week) and moved +0.56% on the Q2 beat. Beats on the reported quarter have not reliably paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a beat is expected. It is filed because the guide-implied midpoint ($2.44) is below the $2.50 consensus, so a beat 'against the guide' may be an in-line print against the street.
findings.independence: Q2 beat size: https://www.metatrader.com/tr/news/1562331-woodwards-q2-earnings--revenues-beat-estimates-increase-yy . Same company documents, so not independent.

findings.finding: The China on-highway natural-gas truck business is being exited: it contributed $40M of Q3 sales and roughly 90bps of the 22.1% Q3 industrial margin, the company said Q4 would carry no significant China on-highway sales, and FY27 Industrial loses that revenue against a high FY26 comparison (transportation +40% in Q3).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: China on-highway upside lifted the Q3 industrial margin (+720bps y/y), and the stock still fell. The wind-down was announced on the same call.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because the company disclosed it. What is unpriced is the size of the FY27 industrial growth hole in the initial guide (several % of industrial sales). Net of the rest of the company: power generation (+19%, data-centre demand) and aerospace volume must offset, and the guide reveals that mix.
findings.independence: Company statement on the Q3 call, also in the Zacks summary (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2970274/). Same underlying disclosure.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-16, two days before the print, Woodward announced a reshuffle effective 2027-01-01: the COO (Tom Cromwell) moves to 'Strategic Initiatives' and the COO role will not be backfilled; the Industrial segment president (Randy Hobbs) becomes Chief Transformation Officer for a Lean programme; and a business-unit GM is promoted to run Industrial. The aggregator page shows a -5.77% move beside the item (undated, unverified).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Already in the tape: the 5-day run-up of -6.5% spans it. Filed because a Lean 'transformation' officer and a new Industrial head announced just before the guide may come with FY27 restructuring costs or margin targets on the call. The sign is unknown.

findings.finding: Positioning and guide-setting history favour the long side at the margin. Woodward's last initial guide (FY26, issued 2025-11-24: sales +7-12%, EPS $7.50-8.00) was raised four times to +20-23% and $9.30-9.50, and the stock rose +12.44% on that print. The stock now enters at -27.5% from its high, -13.9% in the week after Q3 and -6.5% in five sessions, with short interest under 2 days to cover, so the derating has come from long selling rather than a short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Initial-guide print 2025-11-24 +12.44%; 2026-02-02 +13.42% on a raise; 2026-07-29 -7.56% on a raise into a high multiple. Reactions are large in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The options market is not leaning this way: a put/call OI of 14 and a rejected but huge put skew say downside is bid. The case is that the bar has been reset lower by a 27% drawdown. If the market expected a conservative-but-beatable guide to be bought, the stock would not be at its post-Q3 lows into the print.
findings.independence: Sentiment downgrade and drawdown context: https://finviz.com/news/420898/woodward-closes-a-record-year-as-fading-tailwinds-put-its-fiscal-2027-outlook-on-trial . Short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/wwd/summary .

findings.finding: On the Q2 FY26 call (2026-04-29) management said that if geopolitical developments affect defense spending and airline traffic, 'we expect them to be felt in fiscal 2027'. That is a pre-signalled caution for the FY27 guide, and TDG's Nov 10 commentary on RPKs, oil and the Middle East makes it more likely to show up. Defense OEM was already -6% in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 print +0.56%. The caution did not move the stock then.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an old statement (snippet_only; the page returned 403), but it was conditional then and the condition has since been met, per TDG. A guide that embeds it would show FY27 aerospace growth well below the +21-23% of FY26.
findings.independence: TDG's RPK and oil commentary (https://finviz.com/news/420365/transdigm-finishes-fy26-at-peak-momentum-but-misses-the-whisper-and-guides-to-slower-organic-growth-in-every-channel) is the trigger, so this partly overlaps the TDG finding. It is kept separate because it is Woodward's own statement.

findings.finding: Capital return is running heavy: $198M of buybacks in Q3 alone (vs $45M a year earlier), ~$700M expected returned in FY26, under a $1.8B authorisation from Nov 2025. That cushions FY27 EPS growth through the share count even if operating growth slows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback authorisation came with the +12.44% print of 2025-11-24.
findings.why_not_priced: Known. Filed because a FY27 share-count assumption in the guide (FY26 ~61.5M) can widen the EPS guide relative to the sales guide.

outside_window.finding: Spartanburg facility for Airbus A350 spoiler actuation targeted operational in 2027, with deliveries the year after; a long-dated growth driver with no window catalyst.

baseline_tension: The counterparty evidence (TDG, Safran) leans negative and agrees with the put-heavy options book, so it is probably partly priced. The long-side argument (a deep drawdown, a conservative-guide history, light shorts) cuts against the skew. I end near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced/disputed): the FY27 bar has one source (Zacks) and the Q4 bar is internally inconsistent ($2.50 vs the $9.34 FY), so the guidance findings were capped smaller: TDG -1.0 to -0.8, Safran -0.8 to -0.6, GE +0.8 to +0.6, Q2 geopolitical caution -0.5 to -0.4
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold its Q3 beat-and-raise): the Q4 beat finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.1
Rule 7 (positioning is the thing to beat; heavy put OI and rejected skew): the positioning long was cut from +1.0 to +0.7
